EMISSION ORDER -- MEASURED REFUSAL, not a near-miss. The ROM puts D0 (0x02139f70) BELOW D1 (0x02139fc8). daObjFallBlock_c.h defines `~daObjFallBlock_c() {}` in the class body, and an in-class inline destructor emits D1 then D0; the only other admissible spelling, out of line, emits D2/D0/D1. Scaffolds change nothing (the two legacy shards carried one each and both are dropped here). So the licensed run cannot be put in ROM order without spelling the destructor out of line, and the cartridge refuses that spelling: config/arm9/overlays/ov098/relocs.txt carries exactly two inbound references to the pair -- from:0x0213c5fc to:0x02139fc8 and from:0x0213c600 to:0x02139f70 -- which are _ZTV16daObjFallBlock_c + 0x40 and + 0x44 off the address point, i.e. vtable slots 16 and 17, the two the header already names. NO instruction in the image calls either address, and no _ZN16daObjFallBlock_cD2Ev exists in the image or in any symbols.txt -- an out-of-line base destructor would make each of the four descendants call D2 and would leave it live. The in-class inline body is the cartridge's form. Same shape daObjFloatBoard_c settled at (notes/agents/roles/writer.md, 'When a subset is the right answer'), and settled the same way here: the licensed set is cut to the orderable 10 and the destructor pair is held out as deadstrip-duplicate against its own ROM homes. The 12/12 evidence is not discarded -- it is preserved in this branch's first commit and in the partial_isolation block below, which records a 12-object PARTIAL-LINK-VERIFIED run whose ROM is byte-identical to the stock control.

PARTIAL PROMOTION, 10 OF 12. All TWELVE functions verify byte-for-byte from this one TU (12/12 MATCH, objisolate clean, reloc-destinations clean, and PARTIAL-LINK-VERIFIED with the full ROM identical to the stock control -- see the branch's first commit, which licensed all 12). D0 and D1 are held out of the licensed run for EMISSION ORDER ALONE, per the daObjFloatBoard_c / ov029/daObjWcObj01_c precedent: they keep their delinks.txt entries and their src/ shards, and this TU's own copies are licensed deadstrip-duplicate against ov098 0x02139f70 / 0x02139fc8. The licensed run is now 0x0213a00c..0x0213a794, ten functions in ROM-ascending order.

KEY FUNCTION IS Kill(), NOT THE DESTRUCTOR. The destructor is inline in daObjFallBlock_c.h, so the key function is the first non-inline, non-pure virtual -- Kill(), vtable slot 31 -- and this TU defines it. That is why this TU emits _ZTV16daObjFallBlock_c and both destructor variants with no forcing scaffold of any kind. tubuild create carried the two scaffolds the legacy shards used (an explicit `p->~daObjFallBlock_c()` in the D1 shard, a stub redefinition of Kill() in the D0 shard); merged, the stub is an outright redefinition of the real Kill() body and neither scaffold is needed. Both removed, 12/12 still MATCH.

UNLICENSED-SYMBOL COUNT, DERIVED NOT COPIED. writer.md's formula `2 x (ancestors + self) + 1 vtable + 1 Vector3 D1` over the real chain daObjFallBlock_c -> dBgActor_c -> dActor_c -> dBase_c -> fBase_c (5 levels) predicts 2*5 + 1 + 1 = 12, and the compiled object emits exactly 12 unlicensed symbols. The queue's `compiler-only:~1`, copied from sibling ArrowSignRight, is not wrong so much as counting a different thing: ArrowSignRight's ONE compiler_only_output row is its homeless D2Ev, and its other eight went to externalized_output while four more stayed unlicensed. Here all 12 are carried by compiler_only_output and nothing goes to externalized_output: _ZN7Vector3D1Ev is deadstrip-duplicate, and _ZTV16daObjFallBlock_c plus all ten _ZTI/_ZTS records are deadstrip-data, because every one of them has a configured ROM home in some module's symbols.txt. (An earlier revision of this entry put the ten RTTI records in externalized_output; that was wrong on both counts -- they are not homeless, and externalized_output would have pinned this entry to the text-verified-only route, since tubuild.py refuses promotion for any entry carrying it.) With D0 and D1 also held out of the licensed run, compiler_only_output is 14 rows: those 12 plus the destructor pair. Every canonical address was read out of config/**/symbols.txt and every relocation out of this TU's own compiled ELF, not assumed from the sibling.

TWO ROWS THE SIBLING ORACLE COULD NOT WRITE, AND WHY. (1) ov098/ArrowSignRight.json records that _ZN7Vector3D1Ev fits neither policy schema because compiler_only_output refuses a symbol with a configured ROM home. That note is now stale: tubuild.py grew `deadstrip-duplicate` for exactly this case -- a FUNCTION with a ROM home another source owns (arm9 0x020072c0) -- and verify accepts it here (`compiler-only : exact deadstrip ['_ZN7Vector3D1Ev']`). (2) ArrowSignRight left its own _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV unlicensed. This class's own _ZTI16daObjFallBlock_c and _ZTS16daObjFallBlock_c CAN be canonical-imported because mwld's one kept copy of them is not in this module at all: ov015 owns both (0x02114874 / 0x0211488c) and ov098's vtable header word relocates across to them. The vtable itself is the one record that stays in this module, so it takes deadstrip-data against its own ov098 home at 0x0213c5bc. All ten RTTI records take deadstrip-data too, each against the module that actually owns it -- arm9 for the fBase_c/dBase_c/dActor_c pairs, ov002 for dBgActor_c's, ov015 for this class's own -- verified row by row against those modules' symbols.txt.

WHY THIS PROMOTES AND ArrowSignRight DOES NOT. An earlier revision of this entry concluded promotion was refused, because it had routed the ten _ZTI/_ZTS records to externalized_output and tubuild.py:5861 refuses promotion outright for any entry carrying that block ('promotion does not yet persist externalized_output policy'). That routing was the error, not the verdict: every one of the ten has a configured ROM home, so each is deadstrip-data in compiler_only_output, the entry carries no externalized_output at all, and promotion is admissible. ArrowSignRight genuinely does stop at text-verified, because its own _ZTI/_ZTS have no owner outside itself to be canonical against. What remains true of the destructor ordering is that it bounds the promotion to 10 of 12, not that it blocks it.
